AnswerRequest.description:
`POST /api/sessions/{id}/pending/{pending_id}/answer` (ACP core §9): an
option for a permission request, or an action for an elicitation, with
the form's content when it accepts.

AnswerResponse.description:
202 to an answer: it is queued for the session's host, and delivered now
or on the host's next connection (ACP core §4.6). The verdict follows on
the session stream as `pending_changed`.

request_id.description: Carried by the host's `answer_result` for this answer.

session_id.description:
Set when the error leaves a session reachable by id (e.g. a session
start whose delivery is unknown: the session was created and may
still start, but the caller has no other way to learn its id).

AttachedSession.description: A session that a host still has an adapter for, reported in `hello`.

AuthSessionItem.description:
One entry of `GET /api/auth/sessions` (kernel spec §3.2): a signed-in
device, most recently used first.

current.description: The session this request came with.

id.description:
What `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` takes: the SHA-256 of the
session's token, never the token.

CancelResponse.description:
`POST /api/sessions/{id}/cancel`: how the open turn ended. Usually
`cancelled`, but `completed` or `failed` if the turn ended before the
cancel reached the agent, and `interrupted` if the session was parked or
closed while the cancel was outstanding, or its adapter exited.

Capabilities.description:
`hello.capabilities`. Deserialized leniently: a capability this build
does not know (a newer host, a minor protocol bump) is skipped, never a
reason to refuse the whole `hello`. The generated schema still lists
`Capability` as a closed `oneOf` (there is no open-ended JSON Schema
equivalent), but that is a description of the known values, not a
constraint hennery itself enforces: an entry outside it is ignored, not
rejected, so a schema-validating client or proxy must not reject a
`hello` on an unknown capability either.

Capability.description:
A feature a host implements, announced in `hello` (ACP core §3.3). The
collector never sends a frame that needs a capability to a host that
lacks it.

oneOf.description: Project enumeration and browsing.
Image content blocks in prompts.
Explicit park (`park_session`).

committed.description:
Highest committed seq per session listed in `hello`; the host
fast-forwards its counters if they are lower (lost outbox).

oneOf.description:
Start a new session: spawn the adapter, `session/new`, then apply the
requested config (ACP core §3.3, §4.3). Completed by
`session_started` | `start_failed`.

committed_seq.description:
The collector's highest committed seq for this session; the host
continues from the larger of this and its own counter (§5.1).

oneOf.description:
Attach a parked, closed or failed session again: spawn the adapter and
`session/load` it with replay suppression (ACP core §4.3, §4.5).
Completed by `session_started` | `start_failed`, like a start.

agent_session_id.description:
The adapter's own session id, from the stored `session_started`:
the host keeps no copy across restarts.

committed_seq.description: Fast-forward the host's counter before the first frame (§5.1).

content.description: ACP ContentBlocks, built by the frontend.

oneOf.description:
Stop the turn in flight: `session/cancel` to the adapter. Completed
by that turn's `turn_ended` (ACP core §3.3, §4.4), whatever its
outcome: a turn that finished first is not cancelled.

Switch one config option of an attached session (`session/set_config_option`).
Completed by `config_applied` | `error` (ACP core §3.3).

The operator's choice for a permission request. Completed by
`answer_result` (ACP core §4.6); it has no collector waiter.

The operator's answer to an elicitation; `content` only with
`accept`. Completed by `answer_result`, like a permission's.

Resolve a typed path on the host, where the filesystem is (kernel
spec §5.2, §5.4): absolute, or `~` / `~/…` for the host user's home.
Completed by `resolved_path` | `error{invalid}`.
Completed by `session_parked{operator}` (ACP core §4.8).
Completed by `session_closed` (ACP core §4.8).

ConfigValue.description:
The value of one config option (ACP `session/set_config_option`): a
select's value id, or a boolean toggle's state.

CreateHatRequest.description:
`POST /api/hats`: a name, 1 to 64 printable characters, unique in any
case, and a `#rrggbb` colour (slate when absent).

ElicitationAction.description: The operator's answer to an elicitation (ACP `elicitation/create`).

EnrollRequest.description:
`POST /api/hosts/enroll` (kernel spec §4.1): a host pairs itself with a
code and the public half of the key it generated.

EnrollResponse.description: 201 to an enrollment: the id the host names itself by in `hello`.

EventDto.description: One stored timeline event, as served by REST and SSE.

HatItem.description:
One hat (kernel spec §5.1): an entry of `GET /api/hats`, and the answer
to its creation and its changes.

default_for_new_hosts.description: The hat newly paired hosts get as their default.

HatResolution.description:
200 to `POST /api/hats/resolve`: the canonical path, whether it exists
and is a directory there, and its hat, with the rule that decided it
(absent: the host's default hat).

HatResolveRequest.description:
`POST /api/hats/resolve` (kernel spec §8): which hat `path` resolves to
on `host_id`, as a session started there would get. The host resolves
the path; `~` and `~/…` are its user's home.

capabilities.description:
What this host implements (ACP core §3.3). `Capability` lists
the values this version knows; an unknown one is ignored, not
rejected (see `Capabilities`). Absent means none.

proof.description:
Proof of possession of the host's key (ACP core §3.5): its
Ed25519 signature, hex, over `hello_proof_message(nonce, host_id,
protocol_version)`, where the nonce is the one the collector sent
in the upgrade response's `hennery-hello-nonce` header.

oneOf.description:
Every state-bearing fact is a sequenced frame: it goes through the host
outbox and is acked (ACP core §3.3).

A rejected request. Not outboxed: a rejection means nothing happened,
so losing it only costs the collector a timeout.

The answer to `resolve_path` (kernel spec §5.4). Not outboxed: a
probe changes nothing, so a lost answer costs only a retry.
`canonical` is absolute, symlinks resolved, with no `.`, `..` or
trailing slash; for a path that does not exist, its deepest existing
ancestor is resolved and the rest normalised by its text.

Sent once per connection after the unacked outbox has been resent.
The collector reconciles `hello.attached_sessions` only after this
frame, so a resent `turn_ended` is never duplicated by a synthesised
one (ACP core §5.2).

HostItem.description:
One entry of `GET /api/hosts` (kernel spec §8): a paired host, revoked
ones included.

connected.description: Connected and reconciled: requests reach it now.

default_hat_id.description: The hat of its sessions that no path rule claims (kernel spec §5.1).

Indexed.description:
Fields the collector may read from a session event. Closed set (ACP core §3.2).

The catalogue extracts (`config_options`, `current_model`,
`current_mode`, `current_axes`) travel together: when `config_options`
is present and not empty, the four are one snapshot of the adapter's
config. An absent or empty `config_options` means "no read-back", never
"the adapter has no config" (a response that failed to parse looks
empty).

config_options.description:
The full config catalogue: the adapter's ACP `SessionConfigOption`
objects, for the UI. The collector stores it and never reads it.

current_axes.description: The current value of every other option, by config id.

current_mode.description: The current value of the mode option.

current_model.description: The current value of the model option.

pending.description: On `pending_opened`: the request's id, kind and option ids.

LifecycleResponse.description:
Result of a park or close: the session's lifecycle once the request took
effect (`parked` or `closed`).

LoginRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/login` (kernel spec §3.2): the owner's password. 204 and
the session cookie on success. `Debug` leaves the password out.

OpenTurn.description: A session's open turn, for the detail view.

state.description: `sent` (not yet acknowledged by the adapter) or `started`.

PairingCodeResponse.description:
201 to `POST /api/hosts/pairing-codes` (kernel spec §4.1): a single-use
code for `hennery host join`, shown once.

ParkReason.description: Why a session was parked (ACP core §3.2).

PasskeyCeremony.description:
200 to the start of every passkey ceremony: registration, login and
step-up. `options` is WebAuthn's JSON, for
`navigator.credentials.create()` (registration) or `.get()` (login,
step-up): its `publicKey` goes through
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON` or
`parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`. The finish names `ceremony_id`.

PasskeyFinishRequest.description:
The finish of every passkey ceremony: the credential the browser
returned, as `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()` gives it. `Debug` leaves
the credential out.

PasskeyItem.description:
One of the owner's passkeys: an entry of `GET /api/auth/passkeys`, and
201 to a registration's finish.

PasskeyRegisterRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/passkeys/register/start` (kernel spec §3.2, plan 3c):
the new passkey's label, 1 to 64 characters.

PathRuleInput.description: One rule of `PUT /api/hosts/{id}/path-rules`, as the operator typed it.

PathRuleItem.description:
One path rule of a host (kernel spec §5.1, §5.2): sessions whose
canonical cwd is `prefix` or under it, by whole segments, belong to
`hat_id`, unless a longer rule covers them too.

prefix.description: Canonical: absolute, no `.` or `..`, no trailing slash.

verified.description:
The host resolved the prefix when the rule was saved; an unverified
rule is the path as typed, normalised by its text alone.

PathRulesRequest.description:
`PUT /api/hosts/{id}/path-rules` (kernel spec §8): the host's whole set
of rules, replacing the one before. The answer is the stored set,
longest prefix first.

PendingExtract.description:
The `pending` extract (ACP core §3.2): what the collector needs to hold
a pending request and validate its answer, without reading the payload.

option_ids.description:
The permission's option ids. Absent for an elicitation, and for a
permission request whose options hennery could not parse.

PendingItem.description:
One pending request, as the collector holds it: an entry of
`SessionDetail.pending`, and the data of SSE `pending_changed`.

answered.description: An answer has been accepted for it (at most one is).

delivered.description:
The host's verdict on that answer, once one arrived. `true` sticks
(umbrella §6.8): a card shows "answered" only then.

option_ids.description: A permission's option ids: the only valid answers.

turn_id.description: The turn it was asked in.

PendingKind.description: What a pending request asks the operator (ACP core §4.6).

oneOf.description: `session/request_permission`: pick one of the offered options.
`elicitation/create`: fill in a form, or decline.

PendingReason.description: Why a pending request was cancelled (ACP core §4.6).

oneOf.description: The adapter withdrew its own question (`$/cancel_request`).

The operator revoked the session's host (kernel spec §4.3): it will
never connect again to deliver an answer.

PendingResolution.description: How a pending request ended (ACP core §3.2).

oneOf.description: The operator's answer reached the waiting adapter.
The adapter was told the question is off (see `PendingReason`).

PendingState.description:
Where a pending request stands (ACP core §4.6): `open`, then
`delivered` or `cancelled`.

SessionBody.description: The body of a sequenced, outboxed session frame.

oneOf.description:
The adapter session exists. Resolves the collector's start waiter.
`indexed` carries the catalogue after the start's config switches
(ACP core §4.3, P-13).

The host accepted a start but could not create the adapter session
(spawn, `initialize` or `session/new` failed). Rejects the start waiter.
The prompt reached the adapter. Resolves the collector's prompt waiter.
An ACP message from the adapter, verbatim in `payload`.

The adapter process is gone and the session is detached (idle reap,
adapter exit, or an operator park). Completes `park_session`.
The operator closed an attached session. Completes `close_session`.

The adapter exited without being asked to (ACP core §2.3). Followed by
`session_parked{adapter_exited}`. The stderr tail is scrubbed.

hennery's own diagnostic that is not state (ACP core §3.2): a failed
re-apply, or update kinds dropped during `session/load` (§4.5).
`note` is a machine code; `text` is scrubbed.

A `set_config` took effect: the catalogue the adapter answered with,
the authoritative read-back (ACP core §3.2). Resolves the collector's
config waiter.

The adapter asked the operator something (ACP core §4.6): its ACP
request verbatim in `payload`, with `indexed.pending`. It waits, with
no timeout, until it is answered or cancelled. Its kind is
`indexed.pending.kind` (the body's own `kind` is its tag).

A pending request is over: answered (`delivered`), or cancelled for
`reason`.

The host's verdict on one answer (umbrella §6.8): `delivered` if the
adapter was still waiting for it. A delivered answer is followed by
`pending_resolved{delivered}`.

SessionCatalog.description:
A session's config catalogue and its current values: `GET
/api/sessions/{id}/catalog`, the answer to `POST …/config`, and the data
of the SSE `catalog_changed` message (ACP core §9). Commands, plan and
usage join it with the plans that produce them.

config_options.description: The adapter's ACP `SessionConfigOption` objects, as last reported.

SessionDetail.description:
`GET /api/sessions/{id}` (ACP core §9): the list item, the open turn and
the pending requests still open.

pending.description: Open pending requests, oldest first: what the operator can answer.

presumed_parked.description:
Parked only because its host has been offline past the threshold
(ACP core §5.3); the host may still be running it.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /api/setup` (kernel spec §3.1): the one-time owner setup, with the
token from the setup link. `Debug` leaves the password out.

default_hat_name.description:
The default hat's name (kernel spec §3.1), 1 to 64 printable
characters. Absent: it stays "Personal".

public_url.description: `https://…`, or `http://` to a loopback address; an origin only.

SetupResponse.description:
201 to a setup: the owner is created and signed in (the session cookie
is set), and `public_url` is stored as this origin.

StartSessionRequest.description: `POST /api/sessions` (ACP core §9): `{host_id, agent, cwd, model?, mode?, axes?}`.

StepUpRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/step-up/password` (kernel spec §3.4): the owner's
password again, within a session. 204 on success. `Debug` leaves the
password out.

TurnOutcome.description: How a turn ended. Exactly one `turn_ended` per accepted turn (ACP core §4.4).

UpdateHatRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/hats/{id}`: absent fields stay as they are.
`default_for_new_hosts` can only be `true`: a hat stops being that
default when another takes its place.

UpdateHostRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/hosts/{id}` (kernel spec §4.3, §8): rename a host, or change
its default hat. Absent fields stay as they are.
